review.summary: Attempt 5 of the regression-and-governance chunk is backed by real, current-source evidence and closes four of the six attempt-04 lows in source, not prose. Verified directly: docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-regression-and-governance-attempt-05.checks.json records phase 19, source_sha256 22764b50… (identical to the reviewed source), source_unchanged true, passed true, and 27 commands whose order and content match tools/check_phase.py commands_for(19):71-91 exactly, every exit_code 0 and timeout false. The gate now runs the privacy receipt check (check_phase.py:73 → {"receiptFresh": true, "privateScanReexecuted": false, "gitVisibleFilesChecked": 1701}), test_ci.py (check_phase.py:85 → 32 tests ok), test_review_phase.py (48 tests ok), test_g25* (24 tests ok), and five Rust runs (1.89/1.99 red-team, 1.99 json-unification, 1.89/1.99 red-team-json-unification; fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/test --examples/doc all 0, 115–175 s each). docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.99.0-all-round5.json shares rustInputsSha256 ba2e9883… with the gate's red-team-json-unification receipt, so the all-feature combination is also executed against the current Rust inputs; docs/checks/phase-19-python-preflight.json records the full suite (311 tests, OK, 1 skip) at the same source; docs/checks/phase-19-private-material.json is schemaVersion 2 at the same source with 0 selected-value matches, 0 new tenant occurrences and explicit limitations. Regression substance is sound: tools/g25_fixtures.py:142-238 derives the corpus by traversing exactly the 46 vendor:…:strict-response roots (15,658 one-site mutations, 184 format nodes, 138 enums, 55 projection fields), records skipped null union branches instead of dropping them (:126-134), and crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:62-128 rebinds casesSha256 to the exact cases.json bytes, asserts oracle agreement in Mode::Request against both the strict and public roots, asserts both response modes, checks wire preservation and a typed roundtrip; tools/test_g25_generation.py:235-238 fails closed if any TypeScript-accepted document is rejected by the response policy, which closes the dangerous direction of residual strictness that tools/g25_report.py:42-53 does not count. Governance is genuinely enforced rather than documented: review_phase.py binds score→prompt→CLI envelope→checks snapshot (:191-225), recomputes the decision, requires the full attempt sequence (:84-103), enumerates reviewed-but-undeclared chunks and requires each declared chunk's highest attempt to verify against the current fingerprint before advancement (:228-273), resolves scope evidence before writing any snapshot (:356-370), and keeps CLI diagnostics private at 0600. test_ci.py:44-65 now binds the documented CI gate phase to the workflow's actual --phase, and :113-127 binds the 48-job Rust matrix and 49 total jobs to docs/CI.md and docs/RELEASE.md. Deficiencies are governance-edge and code-quality items, not correctness: the fifth-attempt exception at review_phase.py:79 relaxes the total without retaining any per-category floor, so a total of 41 with one category at 1 would be accepted; g25_report.render() still has no behavioural test and still emits a degenerate "Examples: ." line if residual cases ever become empty; and the `kind` shadowing in the corpus generator plus two compressed-style test files remain exactly as attempt 04 required them fixed. No blocker or high finding.

findings.description: The fifth-attempt exception checks only `review["total"] > 40` and the presence of a finding or limitation; it does not retain any per-category floor. A fifth-attempt review scoring (10,10,10,10,1) totals 41 and is returned as "accepted_with_deficiencies", even though docs/PHASES.md:91-92 states that acceptance requires every category >=8 and the exception text at :94-96 relaxes only the total. tools/test_review_phase.py:335-349 pins the total boundary (41 accepted, 40 rejected) but never asserts what happens to a catastrophic single category on the exception path, so the gap is untested as well as unguarded. This is the path in active use for the current attempt-5 loop.
findings.required_fix: Either enforce an explicit minimum per category on the exception branch of gate_decision (for example all values >= 6, or the same >=8 floor) or record in docs/PHASES.md that the fifth-attempt exception deliberately overrides the per-category floor; add a test in tools/test_review_phase.py that pins the chosen behaviour for a review such as (10,10,10,10,1) with total 41.

findings.description: render() is still not imported or exercised by tools/test_g25_report.py (:7 imports only grouped, ledger, residual_strictness, signature, validate_corpus_binding), so the human-facing report body at :90-226 has no behavioural test; its substantive claims, including the eight bypassed check names at :109-110 and the typed-over-raw precedence paragraph at :118-124, are hardcoded prose with no binding to crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs or contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json. If residualStrictness['cases'] ever became empty, :93-97 and :172-173 would emit "Examples: ." and an empty "Mutation counts: " line rather than failing. This is attempt-04 finding 5 unchanged; the one new test (test_report_discloses_retained_timestamp_refinement) asserts committed document text rather than deriving anything from the implementation.
findings.required_fix: Add tests over render() that derive the bypassed-format name set from the validator's bypass list and the projection precedence statement from contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json and assert both appear in the rendered text, and make render() raise instead of emitting degenerate example/mutation sentences when residualStrictness['cases'] is empty.

findings.description: The mutation loop variable `kind` still shadows the node-kind local inside blocks selected on that same name: `kind` is bound at :184 from schema_node["kind"] and tested at :201, :209 and :213-228, then rebound by `for kind, value in [...]` at :229; the identical shadowing remains in sample() at :51 inside the `if kind == "ZodString"` branch. Behaviour is correct today because nothing reads the outer value afterwards, but this is the file that produces the entire 15,658-case corpus and any later node-kind test added after the loop becomes a silent bug. The related style outliers named in the same attempt-04 finding are also unchanged: tools/test_model_fixtures.py:14-23 has no spacing around assignments and tools/test_ci.py:423 has no space after the comma.
findings.required_fix: Rename the mutation-loop tuple variables at tools/g25_fixtures.py:51 and :229 (for example mutation_kind/mutation_value) so the node kind is never shadowed, normalize the spacing in tools/test_model_fixtures.py:14-23 and tools/test_ci.py:423, and regenerate to confirm cases.json, projections.json and the Rust bindings stay byte-identical.

findings.description: On advancement the milestone record hardcodes `docs/checks/phase-{phase:02d}.json` as the independent_verification evidence, but for rubric phases verify_record validated the immutable per-attempt snapshot `<review>.checks.json` (:224), not that path. docs/checks/phase-19.json is deliberately overwritten by later gate runs (tools/test_review_phase.py:422-424 even asserts that overwriting it must not invalidate the accepted record), so the persisted phase-status evidence pointer can name a file whose bytes were never the verified ones.
findings.required_fix: Record the actually verified checks path (the snapshot returned by check_evidence) in milestones["independent_verification"]["evidence"], and assert the recorded path in the advancement test at tools/test_review_phase.py:385-428.

findings.description: Chunk `--scope-evidence` values are only checked to resolve inside the repository and exist; nothing compares them with the chunk's declared `scope_evidence` in docs/phase-status.json. accepted_chunks (:228-273) verifies the record, prompt and CLI binding but never the reviewed scope, so a chunk could be declared with a broad scope while the reviewer was given a narrower list. The two lists happen to agree for this chunk (the nine declared paths at docs/phase-status.json:3965-3975 match the prompt's "Chunk scope artifacts"), and the prompt is hash-bound, so the divergence would be discoverable but not detected.
findings.required_fix: Compare the supplied --scope-evidence against the declared chunks[].scope_evidence for the named chunk (or persist the scope list in the review record and assert it in accepted_chunks), with a test for a mismatched scope.

findings.description: The corpus coverage test asserts that every one of the 46 roots has a `base` case but never asserts that the base or the per-branch witnesses are actually accepted (`outcome["strict"] is True`). tools/g25_fixtures.py:49-75 only synthesizes conforming strings for uuid, rfc3339, duration and date, so a response root that gains an email, url or regex-constrained string would silently produce an invalid witness; the Rust assertions would still pass because the oracle agrees on the rejection, and every mutation under that subtree would become vacuous. Exposure is limited because :235-236 requires every format and enum mutation to be accepted in response mode, which implicitly proves response-mode witness validity for those 322 cases, but strict-mode witness validity is unguarded.
findings.required_fix: Assert that every `kind == "base"` case and every recorded union/branch witness has `outcome["strict"] is True`, and make tools/g25_fixtures.py raise for any string format it cannot synthesize a conforming witness for instead of falling through to the generic "example" value.

limitations: Read-only review with Read/Glob/Grep and no shell: I could not execute any check, recompute the reviewed-source fingerprint 22764b50… or the checks digest 0c42282a…, or run git. Execution conclusions rest on the recorded commands, invocations, exit codes, per-test stderr listings, durations, and the cross-consistency of timestamps and rustInputsSha256 values across the attempt-05 snapshot and the child Rust receipts.

contracts/compatibility/g25/cases.json and outcomes.json are single-line generated files with 15,658 entries each. I verified the generators, consumers, digest bindings and the coverage assertions in tools/test_g25_generation.py, and relied on the recorded --check exit codes; I did not read every case, so non-vacuity and coverage conclusions are structural and sampled rather than exhaustive.

I scoped this to the regression-and-governance chunk artifacts. crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs, tools/generate_models.py, crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs and tools/g25-oracle.mts were read only far enough to confirm that the regressions and the report bind to real behaviour; those belong to the validation-policy and typed-preservation chunks, which carry their own attempt reviews.

The CI contracts job still invokes tools/check_phase.py --phase 17 --verification-only --contracts-only (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:72), so the new g25_audit/g25_fixtures/g25_report/g25-oracle --check freshness commands and the new Python suites are not executed by remote CI; only the Rust matrix exercises the new regressions remotely. docs/CI.md:143-155 states this honestly and the plan assigns CI wiring to phase 20, so I treat it as a scope boundary rather than a finding.

Two attempt-04 low findings (no behavioural test for g25_report.render() with its degenerate empty-residual path, and the `kind` shadowing plus compressed-style outliers) are unchanged in the current source. docs/phase-status.json:4012-4013 records the maintainer decision to carry round-4 lows to phase 20; I report them again because they are this chunk's own required fixes, not because the disposition is undocumented.

No live service, tenant or registry evidence was examined or is claimed. The 17 reported airs-cli-rs loopback failures on the worf checkout remain unexecuted here, and phase-20 qualification, packaging, publication, tagging and terminal CI receipts are out of scope. Acceptance of this chunk at 44/50 does not imply phase-level acceptance, which requires >=46/50 across all three chunks at the then-current source.
